A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FlashSinkhorn, with matching core algorithms, theoretical results, experiments and Appendices A–H. Text extraction and visual inspection support a reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPU benchmarks, HVP accuracy checks, MNIST/Fashion-MNIST OTDD experiments and flow-cytometry shuffled-regression results.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds profiling measurements, low-regularization accuracy and timing tests, and rectangular point-cloud benchmarks.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 removes the running sum-exp accumulator and explicit normalization/marginal reconstruction, directly scaling the accumulated weighted sum instead. This simplifies the computation of the same transport product. The Sinkhorn schedules, balanced objective and HVP construction remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic point-cloud OT, MNIST/Fashion-MNIST distance and gradient-flow tasks, and Cornell flow-cytometry shuffled regression. The added low-ε and rectangular experiments vary regularization and sample counts within retained coverage; no new dataset or task is evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 20 newly evaluates a pure-PyTorch dense fp64 Sinkhorn reference for forward-value accuracy. v1's dense pseudoinverse reference concerns HVP accuracy. The existing GeomLoss/KeOps, tensorized, OTT-JAX and downstream optimizer comparison sets are retained.

E3.justification: Appendices H.2.5–H.2.6 substantially extend evaluation beyond the retained fixed-iteration benchmarks: smaller ε values, fp32-versus-fp64 accuracy, convergence-budget timing, low-ε HVP checks and sample-count ratios reaching 100:1. Table 6 also adds kernel-launch and tensor-pipeline measurements. These are additional protocols, not established reruns replacing the original experiments.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether smaller regularization harms numerical accuracy or convergence, and whether extreme aspect ratios reduce GPU efficiency. Additional profiling investigates launch fragmentation and tensor-pipeline utilization. These materially expand robustness and mechanism evidence beyond v1's retained HVP parity, update-schedule comparisons and saddle-escape cases.

E5.justification: Existing timing repetition counts, mean reporting, seed disclosures and 72 regression initializations are retained. The new numerical-error tables measure accuracy discrepancies; they do not introduce uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and downstream results are retained. New Tables 6 and 19–23 report 130 versus 854 kernel launches, low-ε forward times of 7.60–7.81 ms, fp32 error of 7.69×10^-4 and default HVP error of 8.54×10^-3 at ε=0.01, and KeOps speedups declining from 13.3× to 8.3× across aspect ratios. These substantially extend the findings rather than establish performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 and Appendix B adopt generalized KL with the additional -Pij+aibj terms, correct the marginal-constraint Lagrangian, and state positive-weight and gauge qualifications. The additional KL terms cancel for feasible balanced couplings. The principal theorems and remaining proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract's contributions and headline 32×/161× speedups remain unchanged. Section 3.1 and the conclusion broaden stated streaming-update applicability from squared-Euclidean structure to separable-plus-dot-product costs, explicitly including normalized cosine distance.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations of low-ε iteration growth and damping-related error, extreme-aspect-ratio underutilization, and the contribution of launches and tensor-pipeline activity to speed. It also specifies supported cost structure and excluded costs. These refine the retained central interpretation of fusion and IO efficiency.

D1.justification: The advertised repository changes from ot-triton-lab/ot_triton to ot-triton-lab/flash-sinkhorn. v3 supplies settings for the added checks and corrects a blanket CUDA-event timing statement to match the already-described framework-specific protocols. Existing hardware, software and downstream implementation details remain.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds ESPFormer and LOTFormer to the related-work discussion. Appendix G.2 explicitly acknowledges that the row-stationary traversal aligns with FlashAttention-2. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata or citation formatting.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section/appendix sequence are preserved. Changes include local explanation and cross-reference edits, the title addition 'on GPU', two experimental subsections, acknowledgements, an impact statement and author–year citations.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from one column to two, with extensive figure and table repositioning. Original Figure 1 is redrawn and split into Figures 1–2, adding a GPU-memory hierarchy panel. Six tables are added, and retained displays are resized and reformatted.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens v1 with low-ε accuracy and convergence checks, aspect-ratio sensitivity, a corrected Lagrangian and clearer applicability boundaries. These improve credibility while preserving the central results. The gains are incremental, and Table 21's unspecified convergence criterion limits the strength of its new full-solve timing evidence.
